definition: A directory service in which AI agents publish and discover each other's identity, capabilities and provenance, so that a multi-agent system can find and route work to the right agent.
details: As agent ecosystems grew, registries emerged as the discovery layer that keeps heterogeneous agents interoperable. Approaches range from centralized publication of descriptors (such as MCP Registry and enterprise directories) to decentralized, self-describing manifests (such as A2A Agent Cards) and cryptographically verifiable, distributed directories (such as the AGNTCY Agent Directory Service). They are typically judged on four dimensions: security, authentication, scalability and maintainability. A registry turns "which agent can do this?" into a lookup rather than a hard-coded integration.
story: Think of a chess player who never commits to a move blindly — they consider the board, try an action, watch what changes, and only then decide what is next. The machine stops just answering one question and starts getting a job done, step by step, checking its work along the way. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Agent Registry.

citation.title: Evolution of AI Agent Registry Solutions: Centralized, Enterprise, and Distributed Approaches
